Guadalajara]] | [[United States national basketball team|Team]]}} }} '''Jerome Clifton Dyson''' (born May 1, 1987) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] with the [[Connecticut Huskies men's basketball|Connecticut Huskies]] before playing professionally in the NBA with the [[New Orleans Hornets]], he has also played overseas in Italy, Israel and China. He was the 2012–13 [[Israeli Basketball Premier League Statistical Leaders|top scorer in the Israel Basketball Premier League]]. He was also the 2017 [[Israeli Basketball Premier League Finals MVP]]. ==Early life and college== Dyson grew up in [[Potomac, Maryland]]'s Scotland neighborhood.{{cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2010/01/08/AR2010010803597.html|title=Connecticut's Jerome Dyson is proud to be from Scotland|last=Giannotto|first=Mark|date=January 9, 2010|newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]|access-date=19 December 2011}} He attended [[Winston Churchill High School (Potomac, Maryland)|Winston Churchill High School]] in Potomac for his first two years of high school before transferring to [[Proctor Academy]] in [[Andover, New Hampshire]] for his final two years. While at Proctor, Dyson matured and was recruited to play basketball with the [[University of Connecticut]] [[Connecticut Huskies men's basketball|Huskies]] under coach [[Jim Calhoun]]. During his freshman season at UConn, Dyson was compared by Calhoun to NBA players and UConn alumni [[Ray Allen]] and [[Richard Hamilton (basketball)|Richard Hamilton]]. During his sophomore season, he and teammate Doug Wiggins were caught by on-campus police in a car with alcohol. He was eventually reinstated. In February 2009 during his junior year, he tore a [[lateral meniscus]] in his right knee in an on-court collision with [[Syracuse University]] guard [[Andy Rautins]]. At the time of the injury, he had started all 24 games for the Huskies, scoring in double figures 18 times and averaging 13.2 points per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/news/story?id=3903478|title=Connecticut's Dyson could be out for year with torn lateral meniscus|last=Katz|first=Andy|date=February 9, 2009|work=ESPN.com|access-date=19 December 2011}} He returned the following season and scored 17.7 points and 4.4 assists per game. In March 2010, the [[Sporting News]] named Dyson their 2010 Comeback Player of the Year.{{cite web|url=http://aol.sportingnews.com/ncaa-basketball/story/2010-03-10/sporting-news-college-basketball-comeback-player-year-jerome-d|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130202204248/http://aol.sportingnews.com/ncaa-basketball/story/2010-03-10/sporting-news-college-basketball-comeback-player-year-jerome-d|url-status=dead|archive-date=February 2, 2013|title=Sporting News college basketball Comeback Player of the Year: Jerome Dyson, Connecticut|last=DeCourcy|first=Mike|date=March 10, 2010|publisher=[[Sporting News]]|access-date=19 December 2011}} ==Professional career== ===2010–11 season=== Dyson went undrafted in the [[2010 NBA draft]] and played with the Cleveland Cavaliers and [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] during the 2010 summer league and preseason before being cut. He then signed with the Thunder's [[NBA Development League]] affiliate, the [[Tulsa 66ers]]. He appeared in 47 games with the 66ers, starting 10. He averaged 15.5 points and 27.3 minutes per game and was the team's leading scorer.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/playerfile/jerome_dyson/career_stats.html |title=NBA Development League: Jerome Dyson Playerfile |work=[[National Basketball Association]] |access-date=17 December 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120223123653/http://www.nba.com/dleague/playerfile/jerome_dyson/career_stats.html |archive-date=23 February 2012 }}{{cite news|url=http://www.tulsaworld.com/sportsextra/article.aspx?subjectid=410&articleid=20111116_235_B2_CUTLIN260964|title=66ers' Jerome Dyson takes on leadership role|last=Henry|first=Kevin|date=November 16, 2011|work=[[Tulsa World]]|access-date=17 December 2011}} Following the season, Dyson was named to the [[United States men's national basketball team]] for the [[2011 Pan American Games]] in [[Guadalajara]], [[Mexico]]. Dyson averaged 11.4 points, including a team high 19 against [[Uruguay national basketball team|Uruguay]]. The team, composed entirely of non-NBA players due to the [[2011 NBA lockout]], finished with the bronze medal. ===2011–12 season=== On December 9, Dyson was among nine players added to the training camp roster of the [[New Orleans Hornets]].{{cite news|url=http://www.sportsnola.com/sports/hornets/578279-hornets-add-nine-players-to-camp-roster.html |title=Hornets Add Nine Players To Camp Roster |last=Rogers |first=Dennis |publisher=Sportsnola.com |access-date=17 December 2011 |url-status=usurped |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120421151432/http://www.sportsnola.com/sports/hornets/578279-hornets-add-nine-players-to-camp-roster.html |archive-date=21 April 2012 }} He did not make their final roster, and returned to the 66ers. However, the Hornets signed him to a ten-day contract on April 10, 2012.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hornets/news/hornets_sign_jerome_dyson__1_2012_04_10.html|title=HORNETS SIGN JEROME DYSON TO 10-DAY CONTRACT|date=April 10, 2012|work=[[NBA.com]]|access-date=11 April 2012}} During his nine-game stint with the Hornets, he would average 7.4 points, 2.1 rebounds, 2.0 assists, and 1.2 steals per game. He would also start for them for one game.{{Cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/d/dysonje01.html|title=Jerome Dyson Stats|website=Basketball-Reference.com}} ===2012–13 season=== On July 27, 2012, Dyson was traded to the [[Phoenix Suns]] in a three-team deal.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hornets/news/hornets-acquire-lopez-and-warrick-phoenix|title=HORNETS ACQUIRE LOPEZ AND WARRICK FROM PHOENIX|date=July 27, 2012|work=[[NBA.com]]|access-date=27 July 2012}} He was waived by the Suns on August 15, 2012.{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/suns/suns-sign-jermaine-oneal|title=Suns Sign Jermaine O'Neal|website=Phoenix Suns}} Later that year, he signed a one-year deal with [[Hapoel Holon]] to play in Israel.{{Cite web|url=http://www.hapoel-holon.co.il//Subject.aspx?articleId=54|title=חולון מפסידה לירושלים|access-date=2012-10-03|archive-date=2014-02-22|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140222180225/http://www.hapoel-holon.co.il//Subject.aspx?articleId=54|url-status=dead}} He was the 2012–13 [[Israeli Basketball Premier League Statistical Leaders|top scorer in the Israel Basketball Premier League]].{{Cite web|url=http://basket.co.il/leaders.asp?cYear=2013&lang=en|title=ISRAEL BASKETBALL SUPER LEAGUE | 2012–13 Season | Regular Season | Statistics – Leaders|website=basket.co.il}} ===2013–14 season=== Dyson played with the Charlotte Bobcats during the 2013 NBA Summer League. After the summer league ended, he signed a one-year deal with [[New Basket Brindisi|Enel Brindisi]] to play in Italy.{{cite news|title=Enel Brindisi announced Jerome Dyson|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/105185/enel-brindisi-announced-jerome-dyson.html|access-date=July 10, 2014|work=Sportando.com|date=August 19, 2013}} ===2014–15 season=== On July 10, 2014, he signed with the Italian Euroleague team [[Dinamo Sassari]] for the 2014–15 season.{{cite news|title=Dinamo Sassari announces Jerome Dyson|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/126616/dinamo-sassari-announces-jerome-dyson.html|access-date=July 10, 2014|work=Sportando.com|date=July 10, 2014}} Here, he won the Italian SuperCup, the Italian Cup and the Italian Championship, in a seven game series against [[Pallacanestro Reggiana]] ===2015–16 season=== On November 23, 2015, he signed with the Italian League team [[Auxilium CUS Torino]] for the rest of the season.{{cite news|title=Manital Torino announces Jerome Dyson|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/182836/manital-torino-announces-jerome-dyson.html|access-date=November 23, 2015|work=Sportando.com|date=November 23, 2015}} ===2016–17 season=== On July 12, 2016, Dyson returned to Israel and signed a two-year deal with [[Hapoel Jerusalem B.C.|Hapoel Jerusalem]].{{cite news|title=Jerome Dyson signs two-year deal with Hapoel Jerusalem|url=https://www.sportando.com/en/europe/israel/206083/jerome-dyson-signs-two-year-deal-with-hapoel-jerusalem.html|access-date=July 12, 2016|work=Sportando.com|date=July 12, 2016}} During that season, Dyson won [[2016 Israeli Basketball League Cup|Israeli League Cup]] with Jerusalem, as well as reaching the [[2016–17 EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]] semifinals. On June 15, 2017, Dyson recorded a season-high 30 points, along with 6 rebounds, 5 assists and 2 steals in the championship final game against [[Maccabi Haifa B.C.|Maccabi Haifa]], leading Jerusalem to win the [[2017 Israeli Basketball Super League Final Four|2017 Israeli League Championship]] after an 83–76 victory,{{cite news|title=Final Four – Winner League Final: Hapoel J-M Vs M. Haifa – Box Score|url=http://basket.co.il/game-zone.asp?GameId=22744&lang=en|work=basket.co.il|date=June 15, 2017|access-date=June 15, 2017}} he was later named [[Israeli Basketball Premier League Finals MVP|Finals MVP]].{{cite news|title=מצטיין הפיינל פור: ג'רום דייסון|url=http://basket.co.il/news.asp?id=15696|work=basket.co.il|date=June 15, 2017|access-date=June 15, 2017|language=he}} ===2017–18 season=== On July 4, 2017, Dyson signed a one-year contract extension with Jerusalem.{{cite news|title=Jerome Dyson re-signs with Hapoel Jerusalem|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/israel/239926/jerome-dyson-re-signs-with-hapoel-jerusalem.html|access-date=July 4, 2017|work=Sportando.com|date=July 4, 2017}} On December 16, 2017, Dyson recorded 29 points, 3 rebounds and 3 assists, including a game-winning layup with 10.9 seconds left in an 88–86 win over [[Hapoel Holon]].{{cite news|title=Winner League, Game 10: Hapoel J-M Vs UNET Holon – Box Score|url=http://basket.co.il/game-zone.asp?GameId=23203&lang=en|work=basket.co.il|access-date=December 16, 2017|date=December 16, 2017}} On January 15, 2018, Dyson recorded a season-high 30 points, shooting 8-for-11 from the three-point range, along with 5 assists and 3 steals, in a 92–78 win over [[Maccabi Rishon LeZion (basketball)|Maccabi Rishon LeZion]].{{cite news|title=Winner League, Game 13: M. Rishon Vs Hapoel J-M – Box Score|url=http://basket.co.il/game-zone.asp?GameId=23221&lang=en|access-date=January 15, 2018|work=basket.co.il|date=January 15, 2018}} During his second season with Jerusalem, Dyson participated in the [[2017–18 Israeli Basketball Premier League#All-Star Game|Israeli League All-Star Game]] and the [[2017–18 Israeli Basketball Premier League#Three-point shootout|Three-Point Shootout]] during the same event.{{cite news|title=אולסטאר: הזרים גברו על הישראלים|url=http://basket.co.il/news.asp?id=17631|work=basket.co.il|date=March 2, 2018|access-date=March 2, 2018|language=he}} He was named three-time [[2017–18 Israeli Basketball Premier League#MVP of the Round|MVP of the Round]].{{cite news|title=מצטיין המחזור העשירי: ג'רום דייסון|url=http://basket.co.il/news.asp?id=17374|work=basket.co.il|access-date=December 19, 2017|date=December 19, 2017|language=he}}{{cite news|title=מצטיין המחזור ה-13: ג'רום דייסון|url=http://basket.co.il/news.asp?id=17476|work=basket.co.il|date=January 16, 2018|access-date=January 16, 2018|language=he}}{{cite news|title=מצטיין המחזור ה-26: ג'רום דייסון|url=http://basket.co.il/news.asp?id=17834|work=basket.co.il|date=April 24, 2018|access-date=April 24, 2018|language=he}} On June 8, 2018, Dyson was named [[Israeli Basketball Premier League Quintet|2018 All-Israeli League First Team]].{{cite news|title=חמישיית העונה בליגת ווינר סל 2017/18|url=http://basket.co.il/news.asp?id=19054|work=basket.co.il|date=June 8, 2018|language=he|access-date=June 8, 2018}} Dyson led Jerusalem to the [[2018 Israeli Basketball Premier League Final Four|2018 Israeli League Final Four]], where they eventually lost to [[Hapoel Holon]]. In 47 games played during the 2017–18 season (played in the Israeli League and the EuroCup), Dyson averaged 16.6 points, 4 rebounds, 3.3 assists and 1.6 steals per game. ===2018–19 season=== On July 8, 2018, Dyson signed with the Chinese team [[Jiangsu Dragons]] for the 2018–19 season.{{cite news|title=【官宣】杰罗姆-戴森正式加盟江苏肯帝亚|url=http://www.sohu.com/a/240036711_461606|work=sohu.com|date=July 8, 2018|language=zh|access-date=July 10, 2018}} However, In November 2018, Dyson parted ways with Jiangsu after appearing in six games due to a thumb injury.{{cite news|title=הפועל ת"א מעוניינת בג'רום דייסון|url=https://www.ynet.co.il/articles/0,7340,L-5456505,00.html|work=ynet.co.il|date=February 1, 2019|language=he|access-date=February 4, 2019}} On February 10, 2019, Dyson returned to Israel for a third stint, joining [[Bnei Herzliya]] for the rest of the season.{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/jerome-dyson-dor-fischer-sign-with-bnei-herzliya/|title=Jerome Dyson, D'or Fischer sign with Bnei Herzliya|work=Sportando.basketball|access-date=February 10, 2019|date=February 10, 2019|archive-date=November 29, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211129004542/https://sportando.basketball/en/jerome-dyson-dor-fischer-sign-with-bnei-herzliya/|url-status=dead}} In 15 games played for Herzliya, he averaged 17.2 points, 3.2 rebounds, 3.7 assists and 1.8 steals per game. ===2019–20 season=== On July 26, 2019, Dyson returned to Italy for a second stint, signing with [[Pallacanestro Virtus Roma|Virtus Roma]] for the 2019–20 season.{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/jerome-dyson-signs-in-italy-with-virtus-roma/|title=Jerome Dyson signs in Italy with Virtus Roma|work=Sportando.basketball|access-date=July 26, 2019|date=July 26, 2019}}{{Dead link|date=January 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }} On February 26 he transferred to [[Fortitudo Bologna]]{{cite web |title=Jerome Dyson è un nuovo giocatore della Fortitudo Pompea! |url=http://www.fortitudo103.it/jerome-dyson-e-un-nuovo-giocatore-della-fortitudo-pompea/ |publisher=fortitudo103.it |date=26 February 2020 |language=it }} that was looking for someone to replace [[Kassius Robertson]] who was injured with the Canadian national team during the [[2021 FIBA AmeriCup]] qualifiers.{{cite news |title=Fortitudo Pompea Bologna will sign Jerome Dyson after Kassius Robertson's injury |newspaper=Sportando |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/fortitudo-pompea-bologna-will-sign-jerome-dyson-after-kassius-robertsons-injury/ |publisher=sportando.basketball |date=25 February 2020 }} ===2020–21 season=== On December 25, 2020, he has signed with [[Spójnia Stargard]] of the [[Polish Basketball League|PLK]].{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/spojnia-stargard-signs-jerome-dyson/|title=Spojnia Stargard signs Jerome Dyson|date=December 25, 2020|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=December 25, 2020}} ==The Basketball Tournament== In 2017, Dyson played for The CITI Team of [[The Basketball Tournament]]. The Basketball Tournament is an annual $2 million winner-take-all tournament broadcast on [[ESPN]].{{cite web |url=https://thetournament.com/players/jerome-dyson |title=Jerome Dyson {{!}} The Basketball Tournament |website=thetournament.com |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180313154016/https://thetournament.com/players/jerome-dyson |archive-date=2018-03-13}} ==Career statistics== ===EuroLeague=== {{Euroleague player statistics legend}} {{Euroleague player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2014–15 Euroleague|2014–15]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[Dinamo Basket Sassari|Sassari]] | 10 || 10 || 23.9 || .353 || .289 || .531 || 2.5 || 3.0 || 1.7 || .1 || 10.2 || 5.9 |- class="sortbottom" | colspan=2 style="text-align:center;"| Career | 10 || 10 || 23.9 || .353 || .289 || .531 || 2.5 || 3.0 || 1.7 || .1 || 10.2 || 5.9 {{s-end}} ===NBA=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | align="left" | {{nbay|2011}} | align="left" | [[2011–12 New Orleans Hornets season|New Orleans]] | 9 || 1 || 20.0 || .396 || .125 || .778 || 2.1 || 2.0 || 1.2 || .2 || 7.4 |- | colspan=2 align="center" | Career | 9 || 1 || 20.0 || .396 || .125 || .778 || 2.1 || 2.0 || 1.2 || .2 || 7.4 {{S-end}} ==Personal== Dyson's mother, Julie, is a pastor at the Immanuel Church of God in [[Germantown, Maryland]].
